title: Casting Renderer Runtime
problem: Nako should support casting, but it needs Renderer Sessions, renderer-control commands, adapter boundaries, and cast-safe transport instead of stretching browser tickets or Transcode Session IDs into protocol-specific playback control.

evidence.summary: Opened the casting renderer runtime lane and ADR 0040, choosing Renderer Sessions plus protocol adapters with Nako-to-Nako cast before Chromecast, DLNA, or AirPlay.

Added characterization tests proving Public Client has Playback Session routes and heartbeat, but no renderer/cast route surface, renderer session identity, target handoff, or command capability fields yet.

Added core Renderer Session and Renderer Command records, durable SQLite/PostgreSQL repository adapters, baseline tables, and contract coverage for registration heartbeat, playback attachment, command claim, and terminal completion.

Added Nako-to-Nako Public Client renderer registration, heartbeat/capability update, controllable renderer listing, command polling/completion, safe DTO/OpenAPI/SDK contracts, and route tests that keep external cast protocols out of this adapter path.

Added policy-checked Nako renderer play command flow that creates a direct-play Playback Session, queues a renderer play command, attaches the session to the renderer, and proves denied policy/control creates no playback, transcode, ticket, or command runtime records.
Added redaction-safe Admin renderer runtime diagnostics, Admin Web contract coverage, and protocol adapter follow-on contracts for Nako non-direct transport, Chromecast, DLNA, and AirPlay.
Closed the casting renderer runtime lane with fresh playback/renderer, Public Client, formatting, whitespace, and JSON gates, leaving external protocol work split to adapter follow-ons.

continue_policy.notes: Casting renderer runtime is complete for Nako-to-Nako casting, renderer sessions, commands, Admin diagnostics, and adapter contracts. Start new bounded lanes from ADAPTER_FOLLOW_ONS.md for non-direct Nako transport, Chromecast, DLNA, or AirPlay.
